stories.body: President Donald Trump said Vladimir Putin had agreed to supply Russian diesel to US and global markets immediately, with further shipments planned in November and thereafter, as the administration seeks to bring down fuel prices amid the Iran war's disruption of energy supplies. The US Treasury is reportedly suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports until April 7, though other Russian assets remain frozen. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the arrangement a gift to Putin and an investment in prolonging the war, while critics in the US and Europe said it reverses years of pressure on Moscow. Analysts questioned whether Russia can supply the promised volumes or whether they would significantly affect US pump prices.
stories.headline: Trump announces Russian diesel deal, drawing criticism from Ukraine

stories.body: Russian forces dropped five glide bombs on residential areas of Zaporizhzhia, killing at least 15 people, including three children, and injuring at least 16 others, Ukrainian officials said. Rescuers continued searching collapsed buildings for survivors as Zelensky linked the attack to reduced pressure on Moscow following Trump's diesel agreement. The strikes came after US, Ukrainian and European officials met in Miami to discuss a possible path toward ending the war, including energy resilience, security guarantees, reconstruction and Ukraine's future security arrangements. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned that the conflict's stalemate risked escalating further.
stories.headline: Russian strikes kill civilians in Zaporizhzhia as Ukraine peace talks continue

stories.body: Indian police detained prominent opposition politicians and leaders of the youth-led Cockroach movement as authorities moved to prevent a planned protest in New Delhi demanding the election chief's resignation. Organizers say the demonstration is driven by opposition to a voter-revision exercise that has removed 130 million names from electoral rolls. Authorities deployed roughly 30,000 security personnel, restricted transport and communications, and detained protesters in several parts of the country, according to reports. Critics compared the crackdown with the 1975 Emergency, while the government banned the protest and sought to prevent participants from reaching the capital.
stories.headline: Indian police detain leaders of the 'cockroach' movement ahead of election protest

stories.body: More than 100 humanitarian, human rights and civil-society groups said that a year after a US-backed Gaza ceasefire was announced, it exists only on paper because Israeli forces continue to kill and injure Palestinians and restrictions impede aid deliveries and reconstruction. The groups said more than 1,400 Palestinians, including at least 327 children, had been killed since the agreement, while hospitals remain overwhelmed and nearly 1.4 million people face crisis-level hunger or worse. Aid workers and medical staff said daily violence, displacement, destruction and shortages have prevented families from rebuilding despite the formal ceasefire.
stories.headline: Gaza ceasefire is 'in name only,' aid groups say, as hunger persists

stories.body: South African jurist Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her work advancing international justice and accountability for war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide. Pillay, a former UN high commissioner for human rights, has served as a judge in major international tribunals and chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. The Norwegian Nobel Committee praised her courage, integrity and commitment to universal legal principles, citing a career that began under apartheid and included work connected to the tribunals for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court.
stories.headline: Navi Pillay wins the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize

stories.body: A shallow earthquake measured at magnitude 7.7 struck southern Panama, damaging buildings and roads, triggering widespread evacuations and producing more than 100 aftershocks. The epicentre was in a sparsely populated area about 200 kilometres from Panama City, but strong and prolonged shaking prompted people to flee high-rise buildings in the capital. Authorities reported damage to churches, hotels, water-treatment facilities and infrastructure, while early reports indicated injuries but no confirmed deaths. The Panama Canal, the country's main airport and a major copper mine resumed or maintained operations, and an initial regional tsunami warning was later lifted.
stories.headline: Powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Panama

stories.body: A confrontation between Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers and a man in New York City, in which the man was shot and wounded while his five-year-old son was in the back seat of his car, has intensified a dispute between federal officials and city leaders. Department of Homeland Security chief Markwayne Mullin blamed New York officials for insufficient cooperation with ICE, while city leaders argued that federal immigration enforcement tactics create greater danger. Newly released NYPD body-camera footage shows officers arriving after the shooting and assisting the injured man.
stories.headline: ICE shooting renews clash between Trump administration and New York City

stories.body: Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito has gained new prominence as a leading judicial defender of President Trump's policies, prompting renewed speculation about whether he may retire. The Washington Post reports that Alito, long less publicly prominent than some other conservative justices, has drawn increased attention through rulings favorable to the administration, praise from Trump and discussion surrounding a new book.
stories.headline: Justice Alito's pro-Trump rulings fuel retirement speculation

stories.body: United Auto Workers President Shawn Fain said he had comfortably defeated his leading challenger in his reelection bid. Fain, whose combative leadership and labor agenda have made him a frequent target of President Trump, announced victory as the union completes an election expected to determine whether its current direction will continue.
stories.headline: UAW President Shawn Fain declares victory in reelection race

stories.body: Spain's Socialist Party is exploring a joint Senate list with parties to its left for the November 29 general election, seeking to prevent vote fragmentation and deprive the People's Party of its current absolute majority in the upper chamber. PSOE and the broader left are discussing the proposal ahead of the October 16 coalition-registration deadline, though negotiations are complicated by the short timetable and unresolved alliances for the lower-house vote. Analyses of the 2023 result suggest a unified PSOE-Sumar ticket could have substantially altered the Senate balance, potentially giving the left a majority rather than the PP.
stories.headline: Spain's PSOE seeks left-wing alliances to deny the PP a Senate majority

stories.body: Spain's Supreme Court is deciding urgently whether descendants of Spanish exiles who obtained nationality under the Democratic Memory Law should be able to vote in the November 29 election. The court had suspended their voting rights while considering a legal challenge, but the state legal service and prosecutors argue that the suspension should be lifted because there is insufficient time to revise the overseas electoral register. Judges are also considering a request by the Iustitia Europa party to suspend the election itself, with a ruling expected under pressure from the electoral timetable.
stories.headline: Spain's Supreme Court weighs voting rights for descendants of exiles ahead of the election

stories.body: Catalonia's ERC and the Basque left-wing nationalist party EH Bildu will renew their Senate electoral coalition for Spain's November 29 election. The parties said the alliance would strengthen their defense of Catalan and Basque national rights, social rights and housing policy while opposing what they describe as a reactionary bloc. The agreement, which follows their joint Senate run in 2023, must be formally ratified before the deadline for registering electoral coalitions.
stories.headline: ERC and EH Bildu renew their Senate electoral coalition as the left realigns

stories.body: Morocco's King Mohammed VI said cooperation with Spain must never be subject to pressure, threats or blackmail, in his first public speech since a migration crisis in Ceuta and days before King Felipe VI is due to visit Ceuta and Melilla. Mohammed VI said the current migration-cooperation model had become outdated, citing legal provisions and court decisions that he said impede the return of minors and people claiming refugee status. He also criticized what he called irresponsible statements by Spanish political and media circles, as tensions rise over a visit Morocco considers diplomatically sensitive.
stories.headline: Morocco's King Mohammed VI warns Spain against pressure ahead of the monarchs' Ceuta visit

stories.body: Thousands of people demonstrated in central Barcelona to demand action on the housing crisis and mobilize support for a general strike on November 11. The protest honored Olga and Maricarmen, women whose evictions and deaths have become symbols for housing campaigners, with demonstrators calling for an end to evictions, lower rents, indefinite leases and stronger public housing. Police estimated attendance at about 3,000, while the Tenants' Union put the number at 15,000. Organizers said they would shift attention from a Plaça de Catalunya encampment toward building workplace, student and neighborhood strike committees.
stories.headline: Thousands demonstrate in Barcelona over housing and call for a general strike

stories.body: Barcelona's economic commission has approved a proposal to raise the property-tax surcharge on tourist apartments by between 50% and 150% from January 2027, pending final council approval in December. The size of the increase would depend on how many tourist-apartment licenses an owner holds, targeting larger operators most heavily. The measure won support from the Socialists, ERC and Comuns, while Junts abstained and the PP and Vox voted against it. City Hall estimates it could raise about €7 million for protected housing, although the city plans to eliminate legal tourist apartments entirely by 2028.
stories.headline: Barcelona moves to raise property tax on tourist apartments by up to 150%

stories.body: People living in an informal camp near the Besòs river have moved beneath a C-31 bridge after recent flooding swept through their riverside settlement, leaving some without clothing, documents or other possessions. The Besòs experienced its largest rise of the century after intense rain, reaching 936 cubic metres per second from less than three cubic metres per second a day earlier. The Besòs river park has partly reopened after a week of closure, but one bank remains shut and debris is still lodged beneath the Rodalies rail bridge, where cleanup planning is continuing. The flooding has highlighted both the vulnerability of people living in the river area and the continuing disruption to metropolitan infrastructure.
stories.headline: Heavy rains leave vulnerable people along the Besòs seeking refuge and disrupt metropolitan transport
